Package hu.bme.mit.theta.solver.smtlib.impl.generic

Class SmtLibDereferenceDecls

java.lang.Object
hu.bme.mit.theta.solver.smtlib.impl.generic.SmtLibDereferenceDecls
public final class SmtLibDereferenceDecls extends Object
A Dereference is an application of the deref uninterpreted function, but -- unlike an ordinary (f x) whose f is a ConstDecl that getConstants finds and the solver declares -- deref has no backing declaration in the expression, so an SMT-LIB solver would emit (deref …) with no (declare-fun deref …) and be rejected ("unknown symbol: deref"). The native Z3 API sidesteps this by minting a FuncDecl per application; SMT-LIB cannot, and it additionally forbids redeclaring one name with two signatures.

This gives every deref signature a canonical function ConstDecl -- cached, so the same instance is used both when collecting the constants to declare and when transforming the application, which matters because ConstDecl identity is reference equality. The solver's existing constant-declaration machinery then declares and applies it exactly like any other uninterpreted function, per distinct (array, offset, index) -> result signature.
